text: In the rain-softened literary district of Lorne Quay, Ellery & Vane confirmed on Thursday that it has acquired the publishing rights to The Glass Cartographer, the much-discussed debut from Mara Selwyn. The acquisition follows a quiet bidding contest that began after private readings in March, when booksellers praised the novel’s shifting cities and tide-born maps. Sources close to the deal said the company secured Northfold and Commonwealth rights for an undisclosed sum, with publication planned for next spring. Founded in 1987, Ellery & Vane has long built its reputation on patient editorial work and elegant first editions, and the purchase fits its recent turn toward high-concept literary fiction. Industry watchers expect the title to anchor the press’s 2027 list.
